newsitem.title: USA: Outright crude price collapse deflates U.S. cash.
newsitem.headline: Outright crude price collapse deflates U.S. cash.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes saw outright losses on the NYMEX futures market eat away at benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on Thursday, deflating prices heading into the long American Independence Day break.

August WTI/Cushing talked late at $19.45-55 a barrel, some 75-80 cents lower than late Wednesday. News in the morning that Iraqi and U.N. negotiators had finalized a still pending aid distribution plan necessary for restarting oil sales worked against the futures complex all session.

Traders said prospects for fresh oil sales under the stalled "oil-for-food" accord heightened after the reports. Most players expect new Iraqi liftings from August, while others hold out the possibility that Baghdad will prolong the process further, setting-up the markets for a huge price jolt in the fall.
On the domestic grade front, Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James ended around a 18-20 cents premium to the marker, the same levels pegged from the early hours Thursday.

Deals were seen in the Midland/WTI sector at discounts of 31 and 32 cents to August WTI/Cushing, steady from Wednesday. Other trades had West Texas Sour/Midland moving at $1.15 below the benchmark, traders said.

Brent-WTI arbitrage spreads remained wider than they have been in recent weeks, with August Brent-WTI at $1.35-40, and September at $1.25-30. The possibilty for North Sea Brent shipments to the U.S. Gulf off the wider arb took some of the steam out of a surging LLS/St. James differential.
Traders said the sour market should see pressure in the near-term, especially if more concrete evidence of new Iraqi oil sales appears.
August WTI/Cushing ended around $1.88-92, a few cents weaker than Wednesday.
